metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots downward in next period; apply mild upward bias to prevent premature correction.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days below 40) after high peaks, model tends to underestimate; add 1–2% upward adjustment for 3–5 day horizon.  
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., +0.5+), model often lags in upward adjustment; delay peak forecast until 2–3 days after sentiment turn.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true values when sentiment is volatile or event-driven; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.3 for 3+ consecutive days.  
- If true outcome deviates >3% from model in first 5 days of forecast, assume model is misaligned with sentiment trend; re-calibrate using sentiment-weighted moving average of last 7 days.
